lesson.sourceStem: A nurse wore gloves, a gown, a face shield, and a mask while providing care. Using CDC’s sequence for removing these PPE items separately, which item is removed first?

sources.title: CDC: Safe donning and removal of PPE

initial.question_stem: A nurse wore gloves, a gown, a face shield, and a mask while providing care. Using CDC’s sequence for removing these PPE items separately, which item is removed first?
initial.key_cue: The question specifies removal of PPE items separately.
initial.why_correct_short: In CDC’s separate-item sequence, gloves are removed first, followed by eye protection, gown, and mask or respirator. Use the prescribed technique to avoid touching contaminated surfaces.

rationales.B: Gown removal comes after gloves and eye protection in this specified sequence. A different CDC method removes gown and gloves together.
rationales.C: The face shield is removed after gloves in the separate-item sequence, using its clean headband rather than the contaminated front.
rationales.D: The mask is removed later by its ties or elastics. Removing it first does not follow this specified sequence.

initial.one_line_fix: Follow the specified PPE technique and local policy; perform hand hygiene after removal and between steps if hands become contaminated.

retry.question_stem: A nurse is removing a used face shield after taking off gloves. Which technique best avoids contact with its contaminated surface?

options.label: A
options.text: Grasp the front of the shield with bare hands

options.label: B
options.text: Lift it away using the headband without touching the front

options.label: C
options.text: Wipe the front with bare fingers before removing it

options.label: D
options.text: Rest the used shield against the uniform

retry.key_cue: The outside of the face shield is contaminated.
retry.why_correct_short: Handling the headband avoids touching the contaminated front. Place reusable equipment in the designated receptacle for reprocessing.

rationales.A: Touching the front can contaminate bare hands.
rationales.C: Wiping with bare fingers brings the hands into contact with the contaminated surface.
rationales.D: Contact with the uniform can transfer contamination to clothing.

retry.one_line_fix: Keep contaminated PPE surfaces away from bare skin and clothing, and perform hand hygiene as indicated.
